conclusion: Retained arenas show no demonstrated improvement over copying in one matched pair (0.37% difference), and remain 6.67% slower than serial. Combined with the one-worker control, this rules out immediate worker transfer as the main explanation for the prepared-path slowdown. Only about 1.1% of process CPU runs in workers; additional main-thread selection, preparation, dependency replay and state bookkeeping overwhelm that small parallel discovery workload. This experiment does not time each remaining operation separately. The later body-specialization loop is still serial and is excluded by the benchmark stop flag.
semantics: Retain all worker pages in enclosing region without moving objects, defer batch collection, synchronize live state then free phase pages. Disabled by default; compiler opt-in only in phased persistent mode.
workload: Frozen 108-file HEAD 479c52587 input; identical compiler/stdlib/input hashes, 169 rounds, fresh cache per run, identical perf task-event recording, no concurrent builds/tests.
